verdict.rationale: PostHog has a documented official MCP server and public API (openapi.json) that let an agent run trends, funnels, retention, and SQL queries, ship feature flags, and inspect stack traces from an editor/agent (posthog-docs-2, 12, 19, 24, 31, posthog-probe-4, posthog-probe-3). Dashboard assembly, sharing, and alerting are documented product capabilities (posthog-docs-3, 25), but the evidence never explicitly shows the MCP/API path being used to assemble and publish a full dashboard end-to-end, and a hands-on community report describes the AI/LLM integration failing on a related task (cohort creation) and causing severe UI slowdown (posthog-comm-8), raising doubts about reliability of agent-driven workflows. Missing for 10: explicit documentation/demo of an agent creating and saving a dashboard object (not just insights/queries) via MCP or API, and independent corroboration that this specific end-to-end flow works reliably.
